newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms Seine-et-Marne bonds at AA minus.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms Seine-et-Marne bonds at AA minus.

text.p: Rating agency Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it had affirmed its AA minus issuer credit and long-term senior ratings for the Department of Seine-et-Marne's bonds.
"The outlook is stable," S&P said in a statement.

"The rating reflects the department's growing and diversified economy as well as its relatively good financial performance, although the debt level remains high because of pressures on expenditure," the agency said.

"The structural strengths of the Seine-et-Marne economy should help the department outperform the average rate of recovery of the French economy as a whole. This will help the department restore operating margins, and ensure that its capital spending programme continues with slower debt accumulation," S&P said.
Seine-et-Marne covers one-half of the Ile-de-France region around Paris.
"The department's population and its economy are developing rapidly benefiting from the proximity to Paris and the availability of space," S&P said.

"The economic base is highly diversified, though the industrial sector remains particularly important. Seine-et-Marne has been hit by the recent recession in France, as reflected in the rise in the unemployment rate, which, nevertheless, remains below the national average. The recent setting up of large companies shows that the department remains attractive and dynamic and should benefit from the economic recovery," the agency said.

"After several large capital programmes, the department has begun to reduce sharply its investment effort since 1995. However, it remains high because of the large infrastructure needs associated with a fast-growing department. As these capital investments largely are debt-financed, the department's debt level increased sharply to 161 percent of operating revenues at year-end 1996, which remains manageable," S&P said.
